title: George of the Jungle
tagline: Swing in. Sit down. Eat up.
about: A good-hearted jungle man raised by apes falls for an heiress and follows her to San Francisco.
cue: Serve the snacks when George swings straight into a tree.
faces: Banana, mango, Greek yoghurt and honey blended thick

    StartersApe's jungle banana breadCinnamon banana bread baked in a loaf tinHow to make it3 ripe bananas150g brown sugar100g butter, melted, plus extra to serve2 eggs1 tsp ground cinnamon250g self-raising flourMash the bananas with the sugar, melted butter, eggs and cinnamon. Fold in the flour until just combined.Pour into a lined loaf tin and bake at 175°C.Cool a little, then slice thick and butter.Safari tropical fruitMango, pineapple, papaya and passionfruit with lime and torn mintHow to make it2 mangoes1/2 pineapple1/2 papaya3 passionfruits2 limes, juiced1 tbsp torn mintPeel and cube the mangoes, pineapple and papaya into a big bowl.Scoop over the passionfruit pulp, squeeze over the lime juice and toss gently with mint.Chill for 20 minutes before serving.Shep's honey chilli peanut brittlePeanut brittle for Shep, who acts like a dogHow to make itAs written, serves 4Roasted peanuts set in a golden honey toffee with a pinch of chilli and sea salt, cooled hard and smashed into shards for snacking.Line a tray with baking paper.Heat 200g caster sugar, 80g honey and 60ml water until it turns light amber, about 8 minutes.Stir in 250g roasted peanuts, 20g butter, half a tsp chilli flakes and half a tsp bicarb soda, then pour straight onto the tray and spread thin.Sprinkle with sea salt and cool for 30 minutes.Smash into shards.MainsSan Francisco cioppino with garlic toastFish, prawn and mussel stew in fennel tomato broth, with garlic toastHow to make it1 fennel bulb, sliced1 brown onion, sliced4 garlic cloves, 3 sliced and 1 halved3 tbsp olive oil1/2 tsp chilli flakes400g crushed tomatoes500ml fish stock400g white fish fillets, in chunks300g green prawns500g mussels, cleaned2 tbsp chopped parsley1 loaf sourdough, slicedSoften the fennel, onion and sliced garlic in the oil with the chilli.Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer.Add the fish, prawns and mussels, cover and cook until the mussels open. Stir through the parsley.Toast the sourdough, rub with the cut garlic clove and serve alongside.Ape's eye fillet with béarnaiseEye fillet, béarnaise, Queensbury rules at the table.How to make itAs written, serves 4Eye fillet seared and roasted to medium rare, sliced with a buttery tarragon béarnaise, crisp potato rösti and garlicky green beans.Grate 800g potatoes, squeeze dry, season and fry as 4 rösti in butter for 6 minutes a side.Sear 4 eye fillet steaks and roast at 200°C to 54°C inside, then rest.Reduce 3 tbsp white wine vinegar with a chopped eschalot and tarragon to 1 tbsp.Whisk with 2 egg yolks over simmering water, then slowly whisk in 150g melted butter.Blanch 300g green beans and toss with garlic.SweetsJungle tree crash coconut puddingCoconut rice pudding with mango and toasted coconut. George not feel so good.How to make it150g arborio rice800ml coconut milk80g caster sugar1 tsp vanilla bean paste1/2 cup shredded coconut, toasted1 mango, slicedSimmer the rice with the coconut milk, sugar and vanilla, stirring often, until thick and creamy.Chill for 2 hours.Spoon into bowls and top with toasted coconut and fresh mango.DrinksShep's jungle smoothieBanana, mango, Greek yoghurt and honey blended thickHow to make it2 bananas1 mango300g Greek yoghurt2 tbsp honey1 handful icePeel the bananas and mango and drop into a blender with the yoghurt, honey and ice.Blend until thick and smooth, adding a splash of water if too thick, then pour into tall glasses with straws.
